newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Taiwan futures index hangs on Taiwan players.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Taiwan futures index hangs on Taiwan players.

text.p: An ambitious plan by Singapore's SIMEX to launch a Taiwan stock futures index was greeted with mixed feelings on Wednesday, but some traders said keen interest from Taiwan investors was a positive sign.

"There are lots of Taiwanese individuals and businessmen who have been inquiring about this. Stock funds from Taiwan could well be transferred here," said one futures trader with a European trading house.
Many of them had been anxiously awaiting the start of Taiwan's planned futures exchange, he said.

The Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) announced on Wednesday it would launch a stock futures and options contract based on the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) Taiwan index, in January 1997.
The index is a market capitalisation-weighted index of 77 component stocks, which represent a sampling of stocks covering 67 percent of the Taiwan stock market.

"The launch of the SIMEX Taiwan Index Futures and Options contracts is in line with our aim to enhance our position as a risk management centre for stock indices," SIMEX executive committee chairman Elizabeth Sam said.
Taiwan bans trading in unauthorised financial products but trading in the SIMEX and Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) contracts would be difficult to block.
The CME is scheduled to start a futures contract based on the Dow Jones Taiwan stock index on January 8.
Singapore traders said SIMEX may gain from Taiwanese investors' penchant for higher-risk investments, also drawing on the pool of investors in the country's unregulated black market.
Politically thorny relations between Taiwan and China have already attracted investment capital to Singapore, and the trend was likely to continue, traders said.
Some industry watchers suggested China's takeover of Hong Kong at midnight on June 30 next year might boost liquidity for SIMEX.
"To place the whole stock index thing in an Asian perspective, Singapore is considered stable and funds could come from Korea, Taiwan, and Hong Hong," another SIMEX futures trader said.
Unlike the unpopular SIMEX Hong Kong MSCI futures index, pitted against the more established Hang Seng stock futures index in Hong Kong, the Taiwan index faces less entrenched competition.
But many cautioned that niggling doubts prevailed about the success of any regional stock index futures contract, noting SIMEX's inactive Hong Kong index.
A trader with a Japanese bank said the popular Nikkei-225 stock futures contract would continue to dominate.
The question of attracting liquidity due to currency exposure -- as Taiwan's dollar is not traded internationally -- and lack of a perfect hedge against the CME, could also sap liquidity.
Taiwan's plans to establish a futures exchange by the middle of next year could also reduce anticipated Taiwanese participation.
Others, caught off guard by the SIMEX annoucement, criticised the timing of the holiday-period launch, citing insufficient time to plan and market the product to customers.

The size of each Taiwan index futures contract will be US$100 multiplied by the MSCI Taiwan index, and the contracts will be cash settled. Trading hours will be 8.45 am to 12.15 pm Singapore time (0045 to 0415 GMT) from Mondays to Fridays, and 8.45 am to 11.45 am (0045 to 0345 GMT) on Saturday.
